clinician.trajectory_summary: An 82-year-old Asian male presented with a 2-month history of symmetrical pitting edema on the dorsum of both hands, tenderness, and restricted movement in bilateral proximal interphalangeal joints, unresponsive to diuretics. Initial lab work showed elevated ESR (118 mm/hour), CRP (6.58 mg/dL), slight anemia, and hyperglycemia. Plain radiographs of both hands revealed soft tissue swelling without joint space narrowing or bone erosion. Treatment with prednisolone 15 mg daily was initiated, leading to dramatic improvement of all symptoms, resolution of hand swelling, and normalization of ESR and CRP within one week. The patient was discharged symptom-free and remained so during a gradual prednisolone taper without any flare-ups.
